title: Notes From a Coastal Town
author: Owen Blake
body:
Every coastal town has a version of the same story: the ones who stayed, and the reasons that kept them.

Here, it's the tide schedule that runs people's lives more than any clock. Boats leave when the water lets them, not when the calendar says to. Conversations happen on porches, unhurried, because there's rarely anywhere more urgent to be.

It's easy to romanticize until you've lived through a winter storm season. But even the locals who complain the loudest never seem to actually leave.
